patches.old_text:
2. Pre-debit notice before each charge

Stripe sends these automatically. Can opt out for fully custom emails, but **all types must be supported** — partial custom is not allowed.

Custom custom emails must include: mandate text, institution/transit number, last 4 digits of account number. Pre-debit email triggered by `charge.pending` event.
patches.new_text:
2. Debit-notification email each time a debit is made; for custom emails, use `charge.pending` as the trigger, without treating it as final debit success.

Stripe sends the notifications automatically. If sending custom notifications, support mandate confirmations, debit notifications, and applicable microdeposit reminders together; partial substitution is not supported. Mandate confirmation is due no later than five calendar days after acceptance and includes the mandate, institution/transit numbers, and account last four. A custom debit notice includes contact information, account last four, and the amount to be debited. The captures do not establish a universal before-each-charge delivery deadline for the debit email. See [[source-stripe-acss-debit]] (https://docs.stripe.com/payments/acss-debit; old raw/stripe-acss-debit-2025.md:168-188; new raw/stripe-payments-acss-debit-2026-11-07.md:179-198).
patches.reason: Directly remove categorical pre-debit timing and fix the old notice-content mixing while preserving the five-calendar-day mandate deadline and all notification types.
warnings: charge.pending is a notice trigger, not the final payment outcome.

patches.old_text: - **Final and uncontestable** — Stripe sends `charge.dispute.created` and `charge.dispute.closed` simultaneously
patches.new_text: - **Bank-final PAD disputes** — no evidence submission or appeal; `charge.dispute.created` is sent when the customer files and `charge.dispute.closed` when the dispute closes. The older capture grouped both events at creation but did not prove simultaneous delivery. See [[source-stripe-acss-debit]] (https://docs.stripe.com/payments/acss-debit; old raw/stripe-acss-debit-2025.md:190-196; new raw/stripe-payments-acss-debit-2026-11-07.md:107-127).
patches.reason: Remove false simultaneous delivery while keeping finality and the distinct dispute windows in adjacent concept lines.

patches.old_text: Private preview. Auto-retry for insufficient funds on subscription or one-off invoices.
patches.new_text: The May 2, 2026 guide labeled Billing Retries a private preview. The November 7, 2026 guide omits that phase label and describes optional automatic Direct Debit retries for failed PAD payments caused by insufficient funds: at most one retry within 30 days of the original attempt, without a debit failure fee for a Stripe-initiated automatic retry. The omission does not establish general availability or account enablement. See [[source-stripe-acss-debit]] (https://docs.stripe.com/payments/acss-debit; old raw/stripe-acss-debit-2025.md:269-271; new raw/stripe-payments-acss-debit-2026-11-07.md:258-264).
patches.reason: Date the old preview label and add the new bounded retry conditions without claiming a release-phase change.
warnings: Current retry release phase and merchant enablement are unverified.

patches.old_text: `expected_debit_date` available on `payment_method_details` for Charges (estimated, not guaranteed).
patches.new_text: T+4 payment success and T+5 Stripe-balance availability count business days **after submission**, which may differ from creation; neither establishes a customer-bank receipt or a guaranteed final outcome. `expected_debit_date` on Charge `payment_method_details` is estimated, not guaranteed. A submitted or processing payment is not final: the November guide distinguishes `payment_intent.processing` and `checkout.session.completed` from the subsequent PaymentIntent or Checkout asynchronous success/failure events. See [[source-stripe-acss-debit]] (https://docs.stripe.com/payments/acss-debit; old raw/stripe-acss-debit-2025.md:111-121; new raw/stripe-payments-acss-debit-2026-11-07.md:266-276,302-311).
patches.reason: Qualify the existing timing table with its submission base and asynchronous payment-outcome boundary.
warnings: A rare late PAD failure can follow PaymentIntent succeeded; see source and existing failure section.

patches.old_text: **Checkout**: `payment_method_types: ['acss_debit']`, mandate options required (`payment_schedule`, `transaction_type`; `interval_description` required for `interval`/`combined`). Optional `verification_method: 'instant'` or `'microdeposits'`. Optional `target_date` (3–15 days; incompatible with `microdeposits`).
patches.new_text: **Checkout (2026-05-02 guide)**: Explicit `payment_method_types: ['acss_debit']` is used for manual method configuration; Dashboard-managed dynamic methods can omit that field, but `payment_method_options` and mandate options remain required (`payment_schedule`, `transaction_type`; `interval_description` for `interval`/`combined`). Optional `verification_method: 'instant'` or `'microdeposits'`; optional best-effort `target_date` (3–15 days, incompatible with `microdeposits`). See [[source-stripe-acss-accept-payment]].
patches.reason: Old guide line 57 supplies the Dashboard-managed exception while lines 61–67 retain mandatory mandate fields. Date the method guidance and preserve the original target-date conditions.
warnings: The 2026-11-07 index does not establish current Checkout variant behavior.

patches.new_text: Returns `processing` when the bank account was instantly verified **or verification was unnecessary**; this is submitted/processing, not final payment success. `requires_action` calls for additional verification, such as microdeposits. Fulfill only after the later success outcome; see [[source-stripe-acss-accept-payment]] (2026-05-02 guide).
patches.reason: Old guide line 669 includes the verification-unnecessary alternative; lines 754–768 separate processing from succeeded and fulfillment.
warnings: Historical payment-state description; the new base-URL index provides no current status semantics.
